author: David Sackrider
title: Gun violence prevention advocates push for stronger state legislation - NewsBreak
text:
By David Sackrider ,
3 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) – Dozens of advocates from End Gun Violence Michigan took to the State Capitol Wednesday to meet with lawmakers and push for stricter firearm safety measures.
In a rally, Wednesday afternoon, leaders celebrated Michigan’s safe storage laws and “red flag” laws.
A report from the State Court Administrative Office found judges removed 407 guns last year via the Extreme Risk Protection Orders created by Michigan’s red-flag laws. Advocates also say that accidental child shootings are down 60% in the state.
“Through programs like Operation Safe Neighborhoods, we’ve made it a top priority to crack down on illegal guns and get them off the streets,” said Governor Gretchen Whitmer (D-Michigan.)
The governor announced at the rally that Operation Safe Neighborhoods has removed nearly 950 illegal guns from Michigan’s streets.
Democratic lawmakers want to take it even further. The Gun Violence Prevention Caucus, chaired by state Rep. Julie Brixie (D-Meridian Township) unveiled a sweeping set of new bills Wednesday morning to do just that.
“These packages are all commonsense laws that the vast majority of Michiganders support,” Rep. Brixie said.
Among the bills are requirements for gun dealers to be licensed with the state, like members of the liquor or cosmetology industries.
“If you want to cut hair in Michigan, do you need a license? Yes. If you want to serve food in Michigan do you need a license? Yes. If you want to sell deadly weapons, should you need a license? Yes,” said Rev. Chris Yaw of the Episcopal Diocese of Michigan.
The package is also looking ban bump stocks and large capacity magazines, increase the age to purchase a gun to 21, and create a three-day waiting period for those looking to purchase a gun.
(WLNS) Rep. Brixie says the bills would also remove a loophole that allows for guns to be carried in gun-free zones, such as churches and schools.
The caucus is also throwing their support behind a bipartisan package of bills to require police serve personal protection orders free of charge. Currently, victims are required to either serve the orders to the person they are trying to get away from themselves or ask a friend or family member to do so on their behalf.
“No one should one should ever have to deliver a personal protection order to the person they’re afraid of and trying to be protected from,” said Audriana Buchana Cronk with the First Step Domestic Violence Shelter.
Even with the pressure from community activists, Rep. Brixie told 6 News the package focused on personal protective orders may be the only bills that will survive the Republican-controlled House of Representatives.
“It’s important for us though to work on these bills now,” she said. “We did a lot of work drafting these based on the recommendations of the Ending Gun Violence Task Force, and we expect that there will be a change in power in the legislature later this fall, and so, I look forward to re-introduce these bills next year and have it passed.”
